children: Investors slightly cut back their expectations of the Bank of England increasing interest rates over the coming months after the latest U.K. inflation data showed few signs of second-round inflation effects. Annual core inflation stayed unchanged at 2.6% in August, suggesting domestic inflation pressures remain steady. "The absence of clear second-round [inflation] effects gives policymakers room to avoid overreacting," Tickmill Group's Patrick Munnelly says in a note. Markets see an 19% chance of a BOE rate increase at Thursday's policy decision, down from 33% probability priced in on Tuesday, LSEG data show. Nonetheless, investors still fully price in four BOE rate increases over the coming year. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)
